title: Names, owners, and remembered state
description: Trace lexical ownership, create call frames, share state within services, measure lookup, and prepare distinct deferred callbacks.

learned: Find the nearest owner rather than the most recently assigned value.
Use definition scope, not caller scope, for a function's free names.
Share one binding within a service while keeping factory instances independent.
Measure actual membership probes in an explicit frame model.
recap.invariant: Every frame already passed lacks the requested name; the first hit owns that lookup.
recap.complexity: Depth d requires at most d membership probes in the explicit finite acyclic frame model. Drawing is excluded; this is not CPython variable-access cost.
recap.common_mistake: Confusing caller scope with lexical scope or sharing one loop binding among all deferred callbacks.
in_real_programs: Python nonlocal rebinds an existing enclosing function variable.

retrieval.question: Module 1: what distinguishes returning a function from returning its current result?
retrieval.answer: A function can be invoked later with new inputs; its current result is just the value from one invocation.

exercises.title: Build: find the binding owner
exercises.prompt_md: Repair `locate(frames, current, name)` to return `(value, owner_index)` from the first frame on the parent chain containing `name`. A present value can be None, False, or zero. If no frame binds the name, raise NameError. Inputs are finite acyclic frame lists with valid parent indices; None ends a chain. This small model excludes builtins and Python local-before-assignment rules. Call `show_scope` once immediately before testing each visited frame. Do not mutate the input.

checklist.step: Handle shadowing, missing names, and false-like values
Record every visited scope in order

exercises.starter_code:
def locate(frames, current, name):
    while current is not None:
        show_scope(frames,current,name)
        bindings=frames[current]["bindings"]
        if name in bindings:
            return bindings[name],current
        break  # continue to the parent on a miss
    raise NameError(name)
from scimigo import canvas, figure, frame, text

def show_scope(frames, current, name):
    canvas(360, 480)
    shown = [{"id":str(i), "label":"Frame "+str(i),
              "parent":str(f["parent"]) if f["parent"] is not None else None,
              "bindings":[{"name":k,"value":str(v)} for k,v in f["bindings"].items()]}
             for i,f in enumerate(frames)]
    figure("environment_diagram", x=0,y=0,width=360,height=440,
           frames=shown, frame_width=240,
           highlights={"frames":{str(current):"current"}})
    text(12,465,"Probe "+name+" in frame "+str(current),size=16)
    frame()

frames=[{"bindings":{"offset":80},"parent":None},
        {"bindings":{"offset":6},"parent":0},
        {"bindings":{"reading":3},"parent":1}]
try:
    print(locate(frames,2,"offset"))
except NameError:
    print("Offset was not found by this lookup.")

exercises.title: Trace: definition scope or caller scope?
exercises.prompt_md: Implement `call_frame(function, caller, arguments)` for this explicit model. The function record has unique `params` and its defining `parent` index. Inputs have matching arity. Return a fresh frame record with those parameter bindings and the defining parent; the caller index is context, not a replacement parent. Do not change the function or arguments. Call `show_call` with the actual new frame before returning. The helper draws its parameter bindings and parent link; the parent's own bindings are omitted. In the demo, the definition environment has offset 6 and the caller has offset 80; predict the result of adding the new reading 3 to the offset reached through its parent.

questions.prompt: Which result follows from the defining offset and the new reading?

choices.why: That would use the caller's offset, which is not the lexical owner.
That is the offset alone, without the reading.
The defining offset is 6 and the reading is 3.

checklist.step: Bind fresh parameters and preserve the defining parent
Draw the new frame and its actual parent

def call_frame(function, caller, arguments):
    created={"bindings":dict(zip(function["params"],arguments)),"parent":caller}
    show_call(created)
    return created
from scimigo import canvas, figure, frame, text

def show_call(created):
    canvas(360,320)
    owner=created["parent"]
    figure("environment_diagram",x=0,y=0,width=360,height=275,frame_width=240,
           frames=[{"id":"owner","label":"Definition environment "+str(owner),"bindings":[{"name":"…","value":"omitted"}]},
                   {"id":"call","label":"Fresh call","parent":"owner",
                    "bindings":[{"name":k,"value":str(v)} for k,v in created["bindings"].items()]}])
    text(12,305,"Parent = definition environment "+str(owner),size=16)
    frame()

function={"params":["reading"],"parent":1}
created=call_frame(function,2,[3])
offsets={1:6,2:80}
print(created["bindings"]["reading"]+offsets[created["parent"]])

exercises.title: Implement: one box, three operations
exercises.prompt_md: Complete `make_box(start)` returning `(change, read, reset)`. Change accepts an integer delta and returns the updated total. Read returns it without changing it. Reset restores the original start and returns it. All three operations from one factory call must agree on the current total; separate factory calls must remain independent. Each operation calls `show_box(operation, start, total)` after its effect, using operation names change, read, and reset.

checklist.step: Share state within each box and isolate different boxes
Draw actual shared values after every operation

exercises.starter_code:
def make_box(start):
    total=start
    def change(delta):
        result=start+delta  # preserve accumulated changes instead
        show_box("change",start,result)
        return result
    def read():
        show_box("read",start,total)
        return total
    def reset():
        show_box("reset",start,start)
        return start
    return change,read,reset
from scimigo import canvas,figure,frame,text

def show_box(operation,start,total):
    canvas(360,240)
    figure("environment_diagram",x=0,y=0,width=360,height=195,frame_width=240,
           frames=[{"id":"box","label":"Captured box bindings","bindings":[
               {"name":"start","value":str(start)},{"name":"total","value":str(total)}]}])
    text(12,225,operation+": total="+str(total),size=16)
    frame()

change,read,reset=make_box(20)
print(change(5),change(-2),read(),reset())

import random
saved=show_box;show_box=lambda *a:None
rng=random.Random(620)
for _ in range(25):
    starts=[rng.randrange(-30,31),rng.randrange(-30,31)]
    boxes=[make_box(s) for s in starts];expected=starts[:]
    for _ in range(25):
        i=rng.randrange(2);op=rng.randrange(3);change,read,reset=boxes[i]
        if op==0:
            delta=rng.randrange(-10,11);expected[i]+=delta
            assert change(delta)==expected[i],"Changes must accumulate in one shared binding."
        elif op==1:assert read()==expected[i],"Reads must see the current shared value."
        else:
            expected[i]=starts[i];assert reset()==expected[i],"Reset must restore the original start."
        assert boxes[1-i][1]()==expected[1-i],"Separate factory calls must stay independent."
show_box=saved

hints: All operations from one box must agree on one current value.
Compare a second change with a read, then try two separate factory calls.
Keep total in the factory; operations that rebind it can declare it nonlocal.
exercises.solution:
def make_box(start):
    total=start
    def change(delta):
        nonlocal total
        total+=delta
        show_box("change",start,total)
        return total
    def read():
        show_box("read",start,total)
        return total
    def reset():
        nonlocal total
        total=start
        show_box("reset",start,total)
        return total
    return change,read,reset
from scimigo import canvas,figure,frame,text

def show_box(operation,start,total):
    canvas(360,240)
    figure("environment_diagram",x=0,y=0,width=360,height=195,frame_width=240,
           frames=[{"id":"box","label":"Captured box bindings","bindings":[
               {"name":"start","value":str(start)},{"name":"total","value":str(total)}]}])
    text(12,225,operation+": total="+str(total),size=16)
    frame()

change,read,reset=make_box(20)
print(change(5),change(-2),read(),reset())

exercises.title: Measure: count actual membership probes
exercises.prompt_md: Repair `measured_lookup(frames, current, name)` to return `(value, probes)` for a successful lookup. Count each membership test actually performed on a binding table. Return `(None, probes)` on a miss in this exercise. This value alone does not distinguish a miss from a present None; the probe count is the measurement. Use finite acyclic frame inputs and do not draw inside the function. The demo draws your measured results at three depths. This measures the explicit model, not Python interpreter timing.

questions.prompt: For depth d, why can the explicit lookup use at most d probes?

choices.text: It visits each frame at most once
choices.why: Following valid acyclic parent links cannot revisit a frame.

choices.text: It tests every binding in each frame
choices.why: One dictionary membership test is the counted operation, not a loop over all bindings.
This claim is about the model's loop, not interpreter optimization.

checklist.step: Match actual membership operations on hits and misses
Draw the measured counts at all three depths

exercises.starter_code:
def measured_lookup(frames,current,name):
    probes=0
    while current is not None:
        bindings=frames[current]["bindings"]
        if name in bindings:return bindings[name],probes
        current=frames[current]["parent"]
    return None,probes
from scimigo import canvas,rectangle,text,frame

def show_probes(rows):
    canvas(600,300)
    largest=max(c for d,c in rows) or 1
    for i,(depth,calls) in enumerate(rows):
        rectangle(120,25+75*i,430*calls/largest,35,color="#276bb0")
        text(12,48+75*i,"depth="+str(depth),size=17)
        text(125,85+75*i,"probes="+str(calls),size=17)
    frame()

rows=[]
for depth in [2,5,9]:
    frames=[{"bindings":{},"parent":i-1 if i else None} for i in range(depth)]
    frames[0]["bindings"]["key"]=42
    rows.append((depth,measured_lookup(frames,depth-1,"key")[1]))
show_probes(rows)

import random
class Table(dict):
    calls=0
    def __contains__(self,key):
        Table.calls+=1
        return super().__contains__(key)
rng=random.Random(4051)
for depth in [1,2,7,19,53]:
    for owner in [None,0,depth-1,rng.randrange(depth)]:
        fs=[{'bindings':Table(),'parent':i-1 if i else None} for i in range(depth)]
        if owner is not None:fs[owner]['bindings']['key']=0
        Table.calls=0
        value,probes=measured_lookup(fs,depth-1,'key')
        expected=depth if owner is None else depth-owner
        assert probes==Table.calls==expected,"Count each actual membership test, including the successful one."
        assert value==(None if owner is None else 0)
assert measured_lookup([],None,'key')==(None,0)

fs=[{'bindings':Table({'key':3}),'parent':None},{'bindings':Table({'key':99}),'parent':0},{'bindings':Table(),'parent':0}]
Table.calls=0
assert measured_lookup(fs,2,'key')==(3,2) and Table.calls==2, 'Follow actual parent links.'

def measured_lookup(frames,current,name):

        current=frames[current]["parent"]

exercises.title: Mastery challenge: prepare panel badges
exercises.prompt_md: A dashboard configures integer panel prefixes once, then asks each panel to label readings later. Implement `prepare_badges(prefixes)` returning one callable per prefix in the original order. Calling position i with reading x must return `(original_prefix_i, x)`. Configuration may finish before any reading arrives. Later changes to the input list must not alter the prepared behavior. Duplicate prefixes are allowed, and separate setups must remain independent. Empty input returns an empty list. The supplied version creates callables but they do not keep distinct panel behavior. The demo draws the prefixes actually returned by your callbacks.

questions.prompt: What must remain true when readings arrive later?

choices.why: The callbacks must also work after setup returns.
Each panel must preserve its own original prefix.
The callback interface supplies only a reading.

questions.prompt: What does callback position i preserve?

choices.why: That would confuse panels after configuration finishes.
Later list changes must not alter prepared behavior.
Position i must continue to return its original prefix.

questions.prompt: For n panels, what setup and later-call costs fit this solution?

choices.text: Linear setup, constant work per call
choices.why: One small callable per panel; each invocation constructs one pair, excluding drawing and using the bounded-value model.

choices.text: Constant setup, linear work per call
choices.why: The output already needs n callable positions.

choices.text: Linear setup, linear work per call
choices.why: A panel callback need not scan all other panels.

questions.prompt: What goes wrong when two callbacks read one loop binding over prefixes 4 and 9?

choices.why: After the loop the shared binding holds 9, so the first panel loses its 4.
The loop does not stop after assigning its first value.
Defining a function does not run its body.

checklist.step: Preserve each panel after setup and input changes
Draw prefixes actually returned by distinct callbacks

exercises.starter_code:
def prepare_badges(prefixes):
    badges=[]
    for prefix in prefixes:
        def badge(reading):
            return prefix,reading
        badges.append(badge)
    return badges
from scimigo import canvas,figure,frame,text

def show_badges(badges,reading):
    actual=[badge(reading)[0] for badge in badges]
    canvas(600,280)
    figure("array_state",x=0,y=0,width=600,height=230,values=actual,indices=True)
    text(12,260,"Reported prefixes for reading "+str(reading),size=18)
    frame()

badges=prepare_badges([4,9,2])
show_badges(badges,7)

exercises.solution:
def prepare_badges(prefixes):
    def prepare_one(prefix):
        def badge(reading):
            return prefix,reading
        return badge
    return [prepare_one(prefix) for prefix in prefixes]
from scimigo import canvas,figure,frame,text

def show_badges(badges,reading):
    actual=[badge(reading)[0] for badge in badges]
    canvas(600,280)
    figure("array_state",x=0,y=0,width=600,height=230,values=actual,indices=True)
    text(12,260,"Reported prefixes for reading "+str(reading),size=18)
    frame()

badges=prepare_badges([4,9,2])
show_badges(badges,7)
